_comment: Test plan (user 2026-10-25: tests are built alongside the mod). Each feature needs at least `min` DIFFERENT in-game tests passing whose id starts with `prefix` (SCOPE-TEST pass <id>). A new feature = a new line here in the same change (the release tester checks it, and refuses a line removed or a min lowered since the last release). Never lower a min or remove a line to get a push through. Client-only add-on, every Fabric / Forge / NeoForge version in versions/. Each test compares Turbo against plain Litematica in the same game where it can.

features.what: every patch applies on every version
multithreaded chunk builds give exactly the same schematic geometry as Litematica alone
chunks next to the player rebuilt in the background, same result
smooth placement moving: shown moved, rebuilt once stopped, swapped in one frame, same final result
complete copy while moving: the drawn pieces hold every schematic block, kept within the memory limits, freed when deselected, off after an error
Turbo tab: every setting saves, loads and applies right away
a broken patch switches Turbo off for the session with a chat message, no crash, Litematica unchanged
adding a placement (also rotated / mirrored / overlapping) puts exactly the blocks plain Litematica puts into the schematic world

huge, mostly empty schematics are kept in sparse sections: far fewer bytes than dense, the same blocks read, edited, saved and placed, a translated message instead of loading a file that cannot fit, a failing sparse storage switches off with a chat line
Litematica's own display options (layer view, translucent, fluids) give the same picture with Turbo; Turbo never changes Litematica's options

batch drawing (Minecraft 1.16.5 - 1.21.4; 1.21.10 and up skip: Litematica already draws a layer with one multi-draw): far fewer draw calls per frame, the same picture as drawing piece by piece, a changed block shows up, a failing batch switches off with a chat line, a piece whose vertex buffer went missing is left to Litematica while batch drawing stays on
block entities drawn while Turbo rebuilds their chunks never crash the game

next to Sodium (and Iris with a shader pack on): the schematic is drawn, every speed-up works as its own tests prove, no GL errors, no feature switched off, shader switching like plain Litematica and while chunks are building (the buffer builder Iris extends always fills what its format asks for), screenshots; in a run without Sodium these skip
less detail far away: far pieces draw no outline lines with the setting on and some with it off, near pieces draw the same, low memory and an error (with a chat line) bring every outline back
